topics.topic: Module ownership of Authorization header syntax and cardinality validation
questions: Must `deliverer_router` check that there is exactly one Authorization field and that it has the Bearer scheme and required spacing, or does its prohibition on checks mean another module must perform those checks?

Does `deliverer_router` own checking header cardinality, the case-insensitive Bearer scheme and the required single space while extracting the presented token, despite being forbidden to own checks other than request-form checks; or does `deliverer_api` own those checks even though it is assigned only comparison of the token?

How can `deliverer_router` own “the reading of the single `Authorization` field in the Bearer scheme” when it must not own any check other than request-form checks; specifically, which module checks field multiplicity, scheme spelling and case, the single space, and token presence before identifiers and the body?

judgement.divergence: One implementation puts Authorization-field cardinality and Bearer-syntax validation in `deliverer_router`; the other excludes those checks from that module, which the module generator and maintainers observe as different ownership and generated code.
judgement.why: The first passage assigns part of A5 rule 1 to `deliverer_router`, while the second forbids that module from owning the checks required to perform that responsibility.

Every operation except the health answer requires exactly one `Authorization` field. Its value is
   the scheme `Bearer`, compared without regard to case as HTTP defines an authentication scheme, one
   space and the token, compared whole, case-sensitively and in constant time. A request without that
   field, with more than one, or with any other value is refused with the UNAUTHORIZED member of
   = models.RefusalCode before its identifiers or body are examined.

basis:
Every operation except the health answer requires exactly one `Authorization` field. Its value is
   the scheme `Bearer`, compared without regard to case as HTTP defines an authentication scheme, one
   space and the token, compared whole, case-sensitively and in constant time. A request without that
   field, with more than one, or with any other value is refused with the UNAUTHORIZED member of
   = models.RefusalCode before its identifiers or body are examined.

`deliverer_router` is the module that `http_router_backend` generates with its `fastapi_sync_v2` backend, and it
holds only what that backend emits. It serves every route as a table route: the body of a delivery and of a mark
is read as = models.DeliverRequest and = models.PublishedRequest, the token is compared by `check_token` of
`deliverer_api` before the body is read, the project id is judged by its `parse_project_id`, and the route
then calls one operation of `photo_delivery`.

topics.topic: Dependency and data contract for token comparison between router and API
questions: What call or data contract connects the router's extracted Bearer value and application token to `deliverer_api` for comparison, and which module is allowed to depend on which so that comparison completes before identifier and body validation?

quotes:
`deliverer_router` is the module that `http_router_backend` generates with its `fastapi_sync_v2` backend, and it
holds only what that backend emits. It serves every route as a table route: the body of a delivery and of a mark
is read as = models.DeliverRequest and = models.PublishedRequest, the token is compared by `check_token` of
`deliverer_api` before the body is read, the project id is judged by its `parse_project_id`, and the route
then calls one operation of `photo_delivery`. `AuthenticationRequired`, every `DelivererError` and a request whose
body or form the framework refuses are each answered by `refusal_answer` of `deliverer_api`, so every refusal
leaves as M08 (A5 rules 1, 9 and 10). `deliverer_api` therefore cannot import the router back.
judgement.why: The dependency table explicitly directs `deliverer_router` to import `check_token` from `deliverer_api`, and the accompanying passage says the router calls it before reading the body and forbids the reverse dependency.
